page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware specifications include 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 32.0 GB of system memory providing an 8.0 GB per-core ratio, and a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD. It supports modern execution instruction sets including AVX-512, Intel AMX matrix extensions, and cryptographic acceleration through AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark evaluations reflect high single-threaded compute efficiency alongside capacity tradeoffs inherent to a 4-vCPU envelope. Compression benchmarks show strong performance, recording 34.96 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 14.44 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. In contrast, multi-core stress-ng tests and multi-threaded decompression rate in lower percentiles due to the two physical core count. Memory performance registers 44.69 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 22.41 GB/sec in write operations. System benchmarks measure an overall PassMark CPU score of 8395.0, static web throughput of 8.6 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput of 7.86 million operations per second.

Without discrete GPU acceleration, generative AI performance is constrained on larger models, achieving 5.18 tokens per second on 7B LLM text generation, while smaller 135M parameter models execute at 134.95 tokens per second. The server offers cost efficiency by delivering an elevated memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-speed local disk capacity without requiring the compute overhead of larger instance sizes. The hardware profile is appropriate for in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, moderate relational databases, web application servers, and memory-constrained batch jobs.
description: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V virtualization, the instance integrates 32.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per core) and 236 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It supports hardware instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded data compression alongside average overall CPU and memory bandwidth performance, though multi-core compute capability is bounded by the four-vCPU scale. Without a dedicated GPU, AI model processing is practical primarily for lightweight architectures. The E4ds_v7 delivers an advantageous balance of dense memory allocation and local NVMe scratch storage, making it suitable for in-memory caches such as Redis, moderate relational databases, web application backends, and memory-intensive batch processing workloads.
